problem: Object-centric topological navigation methods (RoboHop, TANGO, ObjectReact) choose actions only from currently visible objects' costs, so when the robot starts facing away from the goal or is in symmetric layouts/corridors, it keeps moving along its heading and away from the goal.
motivation: Global topological planning encodes long-horizon structure, but it reaches the local controller only indirectly via costs of visible objects, so the controller has no way to favor progress beyond the field of view. Humans keep a sense of global direction to correct early deviations; a compact directional signal should give the controller the same ability.
key_idea: Compress the global object-level plan into a 2D unit-vector 'intent' (direction to the 2-hop node along the shortest topological path, in the robot frame) and inject it into ObjectReact's waypoint predictor via FiLM, plus BEV-based waypoint feasibility refinement.
insight: A coarse direction is enough: ablation variants (sign-only, concat instead of FiLM, +distance) all reach SPL 65.42-66.54 versus 57.84 for the base, so the policy mainly needs the general direction. Intent acts as a soft bias, since a constant angular bias of up to 20° leaves SPL almost unchanged (30° retains 95%), and gains grow with initial heading offset (up to 87% SPL improvement at 180° offset). The BEV refinement and intent are complementary (BEV alone SPL 68.45, intent alone 66.54, both 76.12).
method: Object-centric topological map: nodes are SAM2/FastSAM instance masks with 3D centroids (monocular depth + poses); edges are Delaunay intra-image links weighted by Euclidean distance and inter-image tracking links (SuperPoint+LightGlue) with zero cost.

Global planning: place recognition retrieves map images, query objects are matched to map nodes, and Dijkstra gives each node's topological distance to the goal; the sub-goal node is the matched node with minimum distance.
Intent definition: the 2-hop node is the first node on the shortest path whose distance strictly decreases below the sub-goal's; intent z=[cos φ, sin φ], φ = bearing to that node minus robot yaw.

Intent-conditioned controller: ObjectReact-style object-distance costmap (sinusoidal encoding projected through masks) goes through a goal encoder; a small MLP maps z to FiLM (γ,β) applied after the goal encoder and before pooling, initialised near identity.
Training: HM3Dv0.2 IIN-HM3D-v3 shortest-path waypoint trajectories with simulator instances/depth; FiLM is trained first with the rest frozen, then the full network is fine-tuned.

Feasibility-aware waypoint refinement: a local BEV traversability map is used at execution to project infeasible predicted waypoints to the nearest free location along their direction or within a local neighborhood; it is deterministic and not part of learning.

Learned-perception yaw estimation: relative rotation from essential-matrix estimation, falling back to yaw approximated from the observed direction of the current subgoal when inliers are insufficient.

setting.backbone: ObjectReact waypoint policy (object-costmap goal encoder) + FiLM intent conditioning, fine-tuned; FastSAM, SuperPoint+LightGlue, NetVLAD as perception modules
setting.training_data: HM3Dv0.2 IIN-HM3D-v3 simulator shortest-path waypoint trajectories; the ObjectReact policy is finetuned on reconstructed maps
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (robot height 0.4 m) with depth, segmentation and pose (GT or learned) and a local BEV traversability map
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints in the robot frame (BEV-refined) executed by a low-level controller
setting.privileged: Prior map built from a reference trajectory; GT-Topological setting uses simulator GT segmentation, depth and localization; GT-PR variant uses GT position for map retrieval; oracle stopping; BEV traversability map assumed available

numbers_note: Custom evaluation on 108 IIN-HM3D-v3 val episodes with ObjectReact-style task variants, not a canonical benchmark. Table rows for Alt Goal/Reverse under learned perception and the Opposite-task results (only in a figure) are not listed here.
results: Under GT-Topological perception IntentReact beats RoboHop, TANGO and ObjectReact-ft on all four tasks, e.g. Imitate SPL 76.12 vs 59.21 (TANGO) and Shortcut SPL 53.86 vs 34.55 (ObjectReact-ft). With learned perception, it still outperforms all baselines even with NetVLAD place recognition, and in the Opposite initial-heading task the gain grows with the offset.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation (Habitat HM3D) on a small 108-episode set; no real-robot experiments
Relies on a known prior topological map and on yaw estimation (a lightweight essential-matrix/fallback), and gains shrink under learned perception
Assumes a BEV traversability map is available, and Alt Goal success rates remain low
